top_story_title: CISA adds a MikroTik RouterOS flaw to the KEV catalog on evidence of active exploitation
top_story_summary: CISA added two vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Friday 2026-09-25, citing evidence of active exploitation. One affects Microsoft Office SharePoint (CVE-2026-65660, CVSS 8.8, code injection); the other affects MikroTik RouterOS. The source reporting names the SharePoint identifier but does not state the RouterOS CVE ID, affected RouterOS versions, or the fixed release - check the MikroTik advisory for the fixed release and the affected version range before planning the upgrade.
top_actions: Inventory every RouterOS device and its running version, then compare against MikroTik's advisory for the affected range and the fixed release; do not assume a version from third-party reporting.
Disable WAN-side administration immediately: Winbox, WebFig, SSH, Telnet, FTP and the API should be reachable only from a management network, enforced with IP > Services address lists.
Upgrade RouterOS firmware to the vendor's current fixed release and verify the image against MikroTik's published hash before loading.

After upgrading, audit the configuration for persistence: unexpected users under /user, entries under /system scheduler and /system script, /ip firewall nat port forwards, /ip socks, unexpected /ip route static entries and changed /ip dns servers.
Replace all RouterOS admin credentials after the upgrade and remove the default 'admin' account; a pre-patch compromise survives the firmware change.
executive_summary: CISA added a MikroTik RouterOS vulnerability to the KEV catalog on 2026-09-25 citing active exploitation; the reporting does not state the CVE ID, affected versions or fixed release, so check MikroTik's advisory.
Treat internet-facing RouterOS as the priority: remove WAN-side management access before the maintenance window, then patch and audit the configuration for persistence.
The second KEV entry, CVE-2026-65660 in Microsoft Office SharePoint (CVSS 8.8, code injection, EPSS 0.012), is not network gear - route it to the platform team against CISA's 2026-09-28 deadline.
Quiet cycle otherwise: no vendor PSIRT advisories and no genuine AI-and-network-devices item in this window.
key_actions: **MikroTik** — Pull every RouterOS device and running version from inventory, and read MikroTik's advisory to establish the affected range and the fixed release rather than inferring one.
**MikroTik** — Restrict IP > Services (Winbox, WebFig, SSH, Telnet, FTP, API) to a management address list and confirm from an external host that nothing answers on the WAN interface.

headlines.title: SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild
headlines.summary: CISA added a MikroTik RouterOS flaw to its KEV catalog on evidence of active exploitation, alongside an unrelated Microsoft SharePoint code-injection bug.
